title: Do Not Be Unevenly Yoked
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Meaning of Being Unevenly Yoked
subpoints: A yoke connects animals to work together efficiently.
Uneven yoking occurs when animals of different sizes or kinds are paired.
This results in the inability to accomplish the work and causes harm to the stronger animal.

outline.title: Identifying the Unbelievers in Context
subpoints: The primary referents are the false apostles who infiltrated the Corinthian church.
These individuals preached a different Jesus, spirit, and gospel.
They promoted self-commendation and judged by outward appearance rather than heart transformation.

outline.title: The Reason for Separation: The Church as Temple
subpoints: Righteousness has no fellowship with lawlessness, nor light with darkness.
The collective body of believers is the temple of the living God.
God dwells in the church in a special, powerful way, distinct from individual indwelling.

outline.title: The Exhortation to Holiness
subpoints: Believers are called to come out from among the unclean.
The motivation is the promise of God’s fatherly care and presence.
The goal is to cleanse oneself from filthiness of flesh and spirit to perfect holiness.

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro examines 2 Corinthians 6:14-7:1, emphasizing the importance of understanding biblical passages within their immediate context. He clarifies that the command to "not be unequally yoked" is not a general prohibition against all interaction with non-believers, but a specific warning against partnering with those who oppose the gospel in the pursuit of God's work. Using the agricultural imagery of a yoke, the pastor illustrates how joining forces with those who do not share the same faith and purpose renders the work of God ineffective and potentially harmful to the believer.

The sermon identifies the "unbelievers" in this context as the false apostles who had infiltrated the Corinthian church, promoting a different gospel and relying on outward appearances and self-commendation. By yoking themselves with these individuals, the Corinthians were compromising their ability to fulfill their divine calling. The pastor argues that God's work must be done God's way, which requires alignment in faith and purpose among those engaged in ministry and spiritual labor.

The primary reason for this separation is the theological reality that the church, collectively, is the temple of the Holy Spirit. While individual believers are indwelt by the Spirit, the scriptural emphasis in this passage is on the corporate nature of the church as the dwelling place of God. This unique presence of God among His people necessitates a separation from unclean practices and false teachings to preserve the holiness of the temple.

The sermon concludes with an exhortation to cleanse oneself from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God. This call to holiness is motivated by the promises of God, who invites His people to come out from among them, promising to be their Father and for them to be His sons and daughters. The ultimate goal is to maintain the purity of the temple so that God may dwell among His people in a special and powerful way.
